```{python}
#| label: fig-bench-walk-peak
#| fig-cap: "The record walk's peak, measured on the OS-less tier over volumes the target did not write, one run each. Reading the enumeration whole grew it with the volume (3,312, 12,144, 39,792 bytes); reading a page of keys at a time does not (1,392, 2,144, 2,160). Three times the volume moves the peak by 16 bytes, where the whole enumeration moved it by 27,648."
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

records = ['8', '32', '96']
whole = [3312, 12144, 39792]   # bytes, the enumeration read whole
paged = [1392, 2144, 2160]     # bytes, a page of keys at a time

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.2, 3.2))
x = range(len(records))
w = 0.35
ax.bar([i - w / 2 for i in x], whole, w, color='white', edgecolor='black',
       linewidth=0.8, hatch='///', label='Enumeration read whole')
ax.bar([i + w / 2 for i in x], paged, w, color='white', edgecolor='black',
       linewidth=0.8, label='A page of keys at a time')
ax.set_xticks(list(x))
ax.set_xticklabels(records)
ax.set_xlabel('Records in the volume')
ax.set_ylabel('Walk peak (bytes)')
ax.set_yscale('log')
ax.set_ylim(800, 120_000)

for i, (whole_bytes, paged_bytes) in enumerate(zip(whole, paged)):
    ax.text(i - w / 2, whole_bytes * 1.15, f'{whole_bytes:,}', ha='center',
            va='bottom', fontsize=7)
    ax.text(i + w / 2, paged_bytes * 1.15, f'{paged_bytes:,}', ha='center',
            va='bottom', fontsize=7)

ax.legend(fontsize=7, loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
